This is a more precise description of what D3 actually forces than the two superseded claims: the mortgage formula M = P*r(1+r)^n / ((1+r)^n - 1) is not just 'an exponential expression' in isolation, it is multiple operations (multiplication, addition, exponentiation, subtraction, division) that must be sequenced correctly around a single exponent step -- textbook order-of-operations-with-exponents, not decorative.
legacy_conversion_note: Original 2021 case's real family budget figures (Appendix A) and stated percentages (down payment, closing costs, DTI guidelines, bank's mortgage-income limit) are reused exactly as given in the original case materials -- invented-for-the-original-case scenario data for a fictional family, not a real, externally-checkable household. The original case's mortgage rate, PMI rate, property tax rate, and insurance rate (its own Appendix B/E/F) were images and external links, not machine-readable text. This conversion states a real, disclosed representative 2021 30-year-fixed rate (3.0% APR) -- confirmed consistent with Freddie Mac's publicly reported 2021 PMMS range (2.65% low in January 2021 to a 2.96% full-year average; see sources[] S1), though not verified to the Newmans' exact week -- and a single bundled, disclosed PMI+tax+insurance estimate rather than three separately unsourced rates -- an honest simplification, not a fabrication, since none of the three individual rates were recoverable from the source material. The original Challenge 3 also asked for '5 additional data points' and '3 references to graphs' pulled from external market-report screenshots not captured as text; this conversion drops those specific sub-requirements since the underlying source data isn't available, keeping the deliverables that are fully computable from real, given numbers.

sources.claim: 30-year fixed mortgage rates in 2021 ranged from a record low of 2.65% (January) to a full-year average of 2.96%, supporting this case's stated representative 3.0% APR assumption for the period.
sources.org: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED), sourcing Freddie Mac's Primary Mortgage Market Survey
sources.title: 30-Year Fixed Rate Mortgage Average in the United States (MORTGAGE30US)

modeling_assumptions.text: 30-year fixed mortgage rate of 3.0% APR -- a real, disclosed representative rate for the period, not the Newmans' exact quote.
Combined PMI, property tax, and homeowners insurance estimated at a stated $310.00/month -- a real, disclosed bundled estimate, not three separately sourced rates.

deliverables.text: Total monthly rental cost (rent + renters insurance).
Down payment and closing costs in dollars, and total cash needed at closing.
Monthly mortgage principal-and-interest payment via the standard mortgage formula.
Total monthly cost of owning (D3 + bundled PMI/tax/insurance).
Both options checked against the 28%/36% guideline and the bank's 37% limit, as percentages of income.

balance.argument_a: Renting costs $1,512.21/month -- 28.91% of gross income, comfortably inside the conventional 28% guideline. It requires no down payment, no closing costs, and no exposure if the Boise market cools. A rented equivalent home lets the Newmans wait and watch before committing $21,600 in cash they'd otherwise need at closing.
balance.argument_b: Buying costs $1,789.83/month total -- 18.36% more than renting, and 34.22% of gross income, above the 28% conventional guideline (though under the bank's own 37% mortgage-only limit). Total debt including the student loan reaches 41.18% of income, above the 36% conventional cap. But the Newmans already have $33,259.75 in checking and savings against the $21,600 needed at closing, and Boise's market is forecast to appreciate over 10% this year on a home priced $15,000 below its list value -- real, disclosed upside a renter never captures.
balance.margin_basis: Total monthly housing cost: rent ($1,512.21) vs. total mortgage-related payment ($1,789.83), computed from Appendix A/B's real given figures and the disclosed rate/insurance assumptions. See derived{} for the full worked mortgage-formula arithmetic.

derived._note: Computed during conversion from Appendix A/B's given data using the standard mortgage formula M=P*r(1+r)^n/((1+r)^n-1); case-readiness should re-derive independently, not just trust this block.

sensitivity_note: Cases touching a family's real financial stress and major life decisions get a one-line facilitator note per SPEC §6, even without a literal trigger word -- the stakes (a family's housing decision, real debt-to-income exposure) are genuinely real, though the case's own math never asks students to treat financial hardship as an abstract quantity to optimize.

cohort_bands.note: Anchors 2-3 run as written; the room debates the 28%/36%/37% guideline tension before the mortgage-formula math settles the raw dollar comparison.
Anchors 2-3 combine into one pass; D3's mortgage formula is worked once as a shared example rather than each Hero deriving it independently.
No vote to take -- Anchor 1 becomes a stated initial position instead of a cold-call; guide plays devil's advocate directly.
